cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **NOT CAUGHT, and clean here is NOT a negative result about the defect.** The sequence COMPLETES, exit status 0, with supervise resolving `expect wsh_read_probe 0x10237a` from the ELF -- so the probe was found and simply never faulted. THE MECHANISM: malloc bounds a capability to the allocator's USABLE size and not to the request, so a crossing shorter than the gap to the next size class stays inside the same allocation and no capability check can see it. This is a property of the allocator's granularity, not of the bug. tools/size-class-audit.py reports this case ABSORBED from the measured request size, and the two agree. The Capstone arms are the discriminating ones here.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.
